pageDescription: jj records all repository operations. More powerful than git's reflog, you can undo/restore any operation. Click an operation to see the command to restore to that point.

divergentBanner.title: Divergent Change detected
divergentBanner.description: has diverged. Find the <1>operation before divergence</1> in the timeline below and use

restore.title: Restore to this operation
restore.undoAvailable: This is the previous operation, so <1>jj undo</1> can be used:
restore.undoNote: undo reverses only the last operation. You can undo the undo itself, so it's safe.
restore.opRestoreNeeded: This is {{stepsBack}} operations ago, so use <1>jj op restore</1>:
restore.opRestoreNote: op restore restores the entire repository to this operation's state. All {{stepsBack}} operations in between will be rolled back.
restore.undoRepeatWarning: Repeating jj undo {{stepsBack}} times won't work
restore.undoRepeatExplanation: Since undo itself is recorded as a new operation, the second undo would reverse the first undo, bringing you back to where you started. Use op restore for going back more than one step.

currentOp.title: Current operation
currentOp.description: This is the latest operation. There are no newer operations.

beforeRestore.title: Verify before restoring
beforeRestore.whatHappenedNote: Operation-level diff. Shows which commits were added/removed/changed. Does not show code content.
beforeRestore.codeDiffNote: Shows file diff of the WC at the operation point. Shows actual code changes.

opDiffVsDiff.title: op diff vs diff
opDiffVsDiff.workflow: Check commit IDs with op diff → view code with diff --from/--to, a two-step workflow.

undoVsRestore.title: undo vs restore
undoVsRestore.undoDesc: — Reverses only the last operation. Since undo is also recorded as an operation, consecutive undos become "undo of undo"
undoVsRestore.restoreDesc: — Restores the entire repo to a specified point. Works regardless of how many operations ago
undoVsRestore.note: Both are recorded in op log, so you can restore again after a restore to go back.

gitComparison.title: Git equivalents
gitComparison.opLog: → <1>git reflog</1> (though jj's is far more detailed)
gitComparison.undo: → <1>git reset / git reflog + checkout</1> (jj is safer and simpler)
gitComparison.opRestore: → (no direct git equivalent; restores the entire repo to a past state)

idGuide.title: Understanding IDs
idGuide.opIdDesc: — Operation ID. Assigned to each operation. Used with
idGuide.commitIdNote: at the time of the operation
idGuide.footer: Commit ID is the same as git's commit hash. In jj, the commit ID changes every time you edit a file, so IDs shown here may not exist in the current
idGuide.footerNote: . Use change ID for tracking as it remains constant.

recorded.title: What gets recorded
recorded.snapshot: — Detects file changes and auto-snapshots. Not recorded if nothing changed.
recorded.footer: All jj commands first check the working copy and record a snapshot if there are changes, then execute the intended operation.
